The diagram presents a line graph displaying three lines representing different variables over time from 2020 to 2023. The x-axis is labeled with years from 2020 to 2023, with tick labels at every year interval. The y-axis on the left side is scaled from 0 to 400 in increments of 50, representing the units in billions of US dollars. The y-axis on the right side is scaled from -200 to 0 in increments of 50.

The diagram shows three lines: a blue line representing imports, a purple line representing exports, and blue bars representing the balance. 

The blue line for imports starts at approximately 200 billion US dollars in 2020, fluctuates slightly, and then increases steadily to around 370 billion US dollars by 2023.

The purple line for exports starts at approximately 150 billion US dollars in 2020, increases steadily to around 180 billion US dollars by 2021, and then remains relatively stable with minor fluctuations, ending at approximately 185 billion US dollars by 2023.

The blue bars representing the balance start at around -50 billion US dollars in 2020, fluctuate slightly, and remain mostly negative throughout the period, ending at approximately -70 billion US dollars by 2023.
